Also known as: Total Spend; Purchase Spend
Definition: The total money paid to suppliers for goods and services in a period.

Also known as: Managed Spend; Addressable Spend Managed
Definition: The share of total spend that is covered by contracts, agreed prices or the purchasing team's control.

Also known as: Off-Contract Spend; Rogue Spend
Definition: Purchases made outside the agreed suppliers or contracts, which are often more expensive and harder to track.

Also known as: Long Tail Spend
Definition: The many small purchases from many suppliers that add up to a small share of spend but take a lot of effort to manage.

Also known as: Procurement Compliance; Purchasing Compliance
Definition: The share of purchases made in line with the agreed contracts, prices and terms.

Also known as: PPV; Price Variance
Definition: The difference between the price actually paid for an item and its standard or expected price. A positive variance means the business paid more than planned.

Also known as: Procurement Savings; Savings Achieved; Negotiated Savings
Definition: The reduction in cost achieved by purchasing, compared with a baseline such as last year's price.

Also known as: Avoided Cost
Definition: The increase in cost that the buyers prevented by negotiating, compared with what suppliers first asked for.

Also known as: Savings vs Target; Target Savings Delivered
Definition: How much of the planned savings has been delivered, shown as a percentage of the savings target.

Also known as: Realised Savings; Savings Realization; Savings Leakage
Definition: The share of agreed savings that actually shows up in the accounts, rather than being lost along the way.

Also known as: PO; PO Count; Purchase Orders Raised
Definition: A formal document sent to a supplier stating what is being bought, the quantity, the price and the delivery date.

Also known as: PO Cycle Time; Requisition to PO Time; Procure-to-Order Time
Definition: The time between a purchase request being raised and the purchase order being sent to the supplier.

Also known as: Requisitions; Purchase Request
Definition: An internal request asking the purchasing team to buy something.

Also known as: PR Approval Time; Approval Cycle Time
Definition: The time taken for a purchase request to be approved.

Also known as: P2P Cycle Time; Procure-to-Pay Cycle
Definition: The total time from raising a purchase request to paying the supplier.

Also known as: Purchase Order Value; Average PO Value
Definition: The money value of purchase orders raised, shown as a total or as an average per order.

Also known as: No PO No Pay; Invoices without PO; Retrospective POs
Definition: The share of invoices or purchases that had no purchase order raised beforehand.

Also known as: Open POs; Outstanding Orders; Open PO Value
Definition: The purchase orders that have been sent but where goods or services have not yet been fully received.

Also known as: Overdue POs; Past-Due Orders
Definition: The purchase orders where the supplier has passed the promised delivery date without delivering.

Also known as: 3-Way Match; Three Way Match
Definition: The share of invoices where the purchase order, goods received note and invoice all agree, so they can be paid without checking.

Also known as: Cost per Invoice; Invoice Cost
Definition: The average cost of receiving, checking, approving and paying a supplier invoice.

Also known as: Invoice Cycle Time; Invoice Approval Time
Definition: The average time between receiving a supplier invoice and paying it.

Also known as: Invoice Error Rate; Invoice Dispute Rate
Definition: The share of supplier invoices that need to be checked or corrected before they can be paid.

Also known as: Prompt Payment Discount; Discounts Taken; Discount Capture
Definition: The share of available early-payment discounts that the business took advantage of.

Also known as: Average Payment Terms; Supplier Payment Terms
Definition: The number of days the business is allowed to pay a supplier after receiving the invoice.

Also known as: Supplier Payment Timeliness; Invoices Paid On Time
Definition: The share of supplier invoices that were paid on or before the due date.

Also known as: Supplier Count; Active Vendors; Vendor Count
Definition: The number of suppliers that were paid or had open orders in the period.

Also known as: Supplier Base Reduction; Supplier Rationalisation
Definition: Reducing the number of suppliers by moving purchases to fewer, preferred ones, usually to get better prices and easier management.

Also known as: Spend with Preferred Suppliers; Approved Supplier Spend
Definition: The share of total spend that goes to suppliers on the approved or preferred list.

Also known as: Top Supplier Share; Spend Concentration
Definition: How much of total spend goes to the largest few suppliers. A high figure means the business depends on a few sources.

Also known as: Supplier Scorecard; Vendor Rating; Supplier Rating
Definition: An overall score for a supplier that combines delivery, quality, price, service and other measures.

Also known as: Supplier Non-Conformances; Supplier Complaints; Supplier NCRs
Definition: The number of problems found with goods or services received from suppliers, such as defects or wrong items.

Also known as: SCAR Closure; Supplier CAR Closure Rate
Definition: The share of corrective actions asked of suppliers that were closed on time.

Also known as: Supplier PPM; Parts Per Million Defective
Definition: The number of defective parts received from a supplier for every million parts received.

Also known as: Supplier Response Time
Definition: How quickly and fully a supplier answers questions, quote requests and problem reports.

Also known as: Supplier Financial Risk; Vendor Risk Rating
Definition: A rating of how likely a supplier is to fail or cause a disruption, based on finances, location and dependency.

Also known as: Diverse Supplier Spend; Small Business Spend; Local Supplier Spend
Definition: The share of spend that goes to suppliers from groups the business wants to support, such as small, local or minority-owned firms.

Also known as: Vendor Onboarding Time; Supplier Set-up Time
Definition: The time taken to approve a new supplier and set it up so that it can be used for orders and payments.

Also known as: Supplier Audits Completed; Supplier Assessment Completion
Definition: The share of planned supplier audits or assessments that were carried out.

Also known as: Tender Cycle Time; RFP Cycle Time; Time to Source
Definition: The time taken from starting a sourcing exercise, such as a tender, to signing a contract.

Also known as: RFQ; RFQs Issued; Quote Request
Definition: A request sent to suppliers asking them to price a defined set of goods or services.

Also known as: RFP; Tender
Definition: A formal invitation for suppliers to propose a solution and price for a larger or more complex need.

Also known as: Bids per Tender; Quotes Received; Average Bidders
Definition: The average number of suppliers that responded to each request for quotation or tender.

Also known as: Competitive Sourcing Rate; Spend Competitively Sourced
Definition: The share of spend that was awarded after comparing quotes from more than one supplier.

Also known as: Spend on Contract; Contracted Spend; Contract Utilisation
Definition: The share of spend that is covered by a signed contract.

Also known as: Contracts Expiring; Contracts Nearing Expiry; Contract Renewals Due
Definition: The number or value of contracts that will end within a given period, so that they can be renewed or replaced in time.

Also known as: Contract Approval Time; Contract Turnaround Time
Definition: The time taken to draft, negotiate and sign a contract.

Also known as: Total Contract Value; Contracted Value
Definition: The total amount agreed in a contract over its full term.

Also known as: Supplier Price Increases; Price Inflation
Definition: The average change in supplier prices compared with an earlier period.

Also known as: TCO
Definition: The full cost of buying and using something over its life, including purchase price, delivery, running, maintenance and disposal.

Also known as: Should Cost Model; Fact-Based Cost
Definition: An estimate of what an item ought to cost to make, built from materials, labour and overheads, and used to challenge supplier prices.

Also known as: Spend by Category; Category Spend Share
Definition: Spend split by type of goods or service, such as raw materials, packaging, logistics or IT.

Also known as: Direct Materials Spend; Production Spend
Definition: Spend on materials and services that go straight into the product being sold.

Also known as: Indirect Procurement; MRO Spend; Non-Production Spend
Definition: Spend on things the business needs to run but that are not part of the product, such as office supplies, maintenance, travel and services.

Also known as: Spend per Buyer; POs per Buyer; Purchasing Productivity
Definition: The amount of spend or the number of orders handled by each buyer.

Also known as: Cost of Procurement; Procurement Operating Cost
Definition: What the purchasing function costs to run, shown as a percentage of the spend it manages.

Also known as: Procurement Return on Investment; Return on Procurement
Definition: The savings delivered by procurement compared with the cost of the procurement team.

Also known as: Catalogue Spend; Catalog Spend; Purchases via System
Definition: The share of purchases made through the electronic purchasing system or catalogue rather than by email or phone.

Also known as: Receipt Cycle Time; GRN Timeliness
Definition: The share of deliveries recorded in the system on the day they arrived.

Also known as: Parts Shortages; Shortage Count; Line Stoppage Due to Shortage
Definition: The number of times production or service was held up because a needed material or part was not available.

Also known as: Rush Orders; Expedite Rate; Premium Freight Orders
Definition: The share of purchase orders that had to be rushed, often at extra cost, because of late planning or shortages.

Also known as: Green Procurement; ESG Spend; Sustainable Sourcing
Definition: The share of spend that goes to suppliers meeting set environmental, social or governance standards.
